newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end higher on strong options trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end higher on strong options trade.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed up in heavy options trade that saw investors selling options to buy stocks, traders said.

The Bovespa index of the 49 most-active stocks .BVSP ended up 1.33 percent to close at 88,161. Volume was high at 2.816 billion reais ($2.681 billion), 2.004 bilion reais of which was in options settlements.
Telebras preferred shares rose 1.93 percent to 100.60 and common shares gained 1.99 percent to close at 97.40.
"Telebras was up because people were selling options and buying stocks," said one trader.
Traders also noted that Telebras also gained from a report late last week by ING Bank that its preferred shares would hit 130 to 150 by the year's end.
The local market also got a boost from figures released by Brazil's Security and Exchange Commission (CVM) showing that foreign investors pumped $949.6 million into Brazil in January.
"The market was happy with the numbers for January. This indicates that people should continue investing here," said one trader.
Some market players, however, warned that Wall Street could see some profit-taking when it reopens Tuesday after the Presidents' Day holiday and that the Bovespa could follow suit.
"If profit-taking starts in New York it could begin here. Our market is up 24 percent since the beginning of the year and we could see some selling off soon," a trader said.
